title: Adversarial Patch Detection for Diffusion Policy Safety
summary: We develop a framework to detect and neutralize adversarial patches targeting diffusion-based policies. By analyzing the diffusion process's vulnerability to spatial perturbations, we propose a frequency-domain filtering mechanism integrated into the denoising steps. The method is validated through controlled physical-world experiments measuring policy success rate degradation under attack.
gap: Current diffusion policy evaluations lack systematic analysis of physical adversarial attacks, leaving safety vulnerabilities unaddressed in real-world deployment scenarios.
approach: Design a spectral perturbation analyzer that identifies anomalous frequency components in input observations. Implement a learnable frequency mask within diffusion policy's denoising network to suppress adversarial patterns. Train using a hybrid loss combining task performance and perturbation invariance.
evaluation: Measure success rate retention on manipulation tasks under white-box/black-box patch attacks. Compare against baselines: standard diffusion policies, input preprocessing filters, and adversarial training. Use metrics including attack transferability rate and physical patch detection accuracy.
